gaps.sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: ___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
gaps.explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

gaps.sentence: She wore ___ heels to the party.
gaps.explanation: 'High heels' is the fixed collocation; 'tall' is used for people, buildings and trees.

gaps.sentence: The smell of hay ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' — remember is not used with an object here.

gaps.sentence: She sat ___ me during the whole flight.
gaps.explanation: 'Beside' means next to; 'besides' means in addition to.

gaps.sentence: We ___ money by cycling to work instead of driving.
gaps.hint: to keep money instead of spending it
gaps.explanation: 'Save money by doing something' means to avoid spending it; 'earn' means to receive money for work.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.
